bfr_space_focus.title: All Eggs in One Rocket
bfr_space_focus.narrative:
You dedicate your entire research programme to the space application. It's a bold bet. You enter a global space innovation competition run by a South Korean health technology company in partnership with Axiom Space.

Your proposal, developing a space-ready BFR device, wins. The prize includes funding and support from space industry partners including Axiom Space.

Winning the competition makes headlines, but those other sectors represented additional impact pathways you've left unexplored.

choices.text: Bring in collaborators to pursue the clinical and sport pathways simultaneously
Stay focused. Use the competition win to accelerate toward flight hardware
Enter the Humans in Space Challenge, a global competition for space health innovation

bfr_operational_testing.title: Beyond the Lab
bfr_operational_testing.narrative:
You design a series of operational feasibility studies to prove BFR works outside controlled clinical settings. You test in a simulated spacecraft cabin (actually a cramped room with restricted movement). You test during bed rest studies at a partner facility. You test in a military gymnasium with non-specialist supervisors.

In each case, the BFR protocols produce comparable results to the laboratory.

You're ready to build the flight hardware.

choices.text: Partner with a medical device company to develop space-qualified equipment
Approach UKSA with the operational evidence for funding

bfr_device_partner.title: Engineering the Solution
bfr_device_partner.narrative:
You partner with Delfi Medical Innovations, a Vancouver-based company that manufactures the world's leading automatic tourniquet systems. Their Personalised Tourniquet System (PTS) is already the gold-standard equipment for BFR exercise on Earth. It provides automatic, personalised pressure prescription with surgical-grade accuracy.

Together, you face the engineering challenge of adapting clinical equipment for space.

The device needs testing. Where and how?

choices.text: Apply to test on a commercial spaceflight mission. The fastest route to orbit
Propose an ISS experiment through ESA's research programme. The most prestigious route
Test extensively in analogue environments first. Bed rest studies, parabolic flights

bfr_uksa_approach.title: The National Space Agency
bfr_uksa_approach.narrative:
You approach the UK Space Agency with a compelling case. You present your multi-evidence portfolio: clinical trials proving BFR's efficacy, sport performance data from Premier League clubs, operational feasibility studies, and your partnership with Delfi Medical Innovations for hardware development.

UKSA is excited. They're actively investing in projects that strengthen UK contributions to international space partnerships, develop national space capabilities, and demonstrate economic and societal benefit.

How do you use this momentum?

choices.text: Focus on getting the device onto an actual spaceflight mission as fast as possible
Build the international consortium and pursue a major ISS study
Use the UKSA backing to also expand the clinical and sport evidence streams
Use UKSA funding to establish a PhD programme in BFR spaceflight countermeasures

bfr_build_team.title: Expanding the Team
bfr_build_team.narrative:
You recognise that one person can't pursue four impact pathways. You recruit a postdoctoral researcher to lead the sport collaboration, and a PhD student funded by a military research council to develop the MOD strand.

The expanded team allows parallel progress. While you focus on the space hardware with Delfi, your postdoc maintains the football club relationships and your PhD student runs military feasibility studies.

After six months, all three strands are producing results. The evidence base is becoming formidable.

choices.text: Bring the evidence streams together into a unified UKSA proposal
Focus on the space strand. The device is nearly ready for testing

bfr_commercial.title: Commercialisation Challenge
bfr_commercial.narrative:
You explore commercial partnerships to bring BFR technology to a wider market. Sports performance companies and physiotherapy chains express interest. A university enterprise team helps you map the intellectual property landscape.

But commercialisation is complex. Patent protection, licensing agreements, quality assurance, regulatory compliance for medical devices, market development. It's a completely different skill set from research.

You need to decide: do you spend your limited time on commercial development, or focus on what you do best, the research that drives everything?

choices.text: Focus back on the research. Space is where the transformative impact is
Pursue both. Delegate the commercial strand to the university's enterprise team
Develop a commercial product alongside the space work. The revenue could fund future research

bfr_international_sport.title: Global Sports Impact
bfr_international_sport.narrative:
You present your BFR research at international sports medicine conferences. The evidence from Premier League clubs attracts attention from football associations, Olympic training centres, and elite sports institutes around the world.

FIFA's medical committee invites you to contribute to their guidelines on post-injury rehabilitation. The IOC's medical and scientific commission cites your research in their review of recovery techniques.

The sport impact is building rapidly. The question is whether to ride this wave or redirect toward the space application.

choices.text: Use the sport credibility to strengthen the space proposal. Show multi-sector validation
Develop the sport impact fully. It may be stronger for REF than the space work
Maintain both. The multi-sector narrative is the strongest impact story

bfr_analogue_testing.title: Simulating Space
bfr_analogue_testing.narrative:
Before risking a flight opportunity, you conduct extensive analogue testing. This includes bed rest studies (simulating the deconditioning effects of microgravity), parabolic flight campaigns (providing brief windows of actual weightlessness), and hypo-gravity simulation (using body tilt and partial weight bearing to mimic lunar and Martian gravity).

The results across all analogues are consistent: BFR exercise with the PTSS device produces meaningful physiological benefits.

The analogue data addresses every concern the space agencies raised. You're now in a strong position to propose a flight study.

choices.text: Propose a flight study on a commercial spaceflight mission
Submit a comprehensive ISS research proposal through ESA
Approach UKSA for funding to bridge from analogue to flight
Present the analogue data at the Spaceflight Human Optimisation Summit

bfr_commercial_flight.title: SpaceX and Beyond
bfr_commercial_flight.narrative:
Your device is selected for a commercial spaceflight mission. The SpaceX Fram2 mission will carry your PTSS BFR exercise device as part of a research initiative studying countermeasures for crew health and performance in space.

The preparation is intense. Every piece of equipment going to space must be tested, certified, and integrated with spacecraft systems. Your engineering partner leads the hardware qualification; you lead the experimental protocol.

The results make international news. How do you capitalise on this success?

choices.text: Secure further UKSA funding to develop next-generation flight hardware
Build an international consortium for a full ISS study programme
Ensure the clinical and sport impact streams are documented alongside the space success

bfr_iss_proposal.title: The ISS Experiment
bfr_iss_proposal.narrative:
You submit a comprehensive proposal through ESA's research programme for a dedicated BFR study on the International Space Station. The proposal is backed by your clinical evidence, sport performance data, analogue testing results, and the PTSS hardware developed with your industry partner.

The review panel is impressed. One reviewer notes: 

"This is the experiment that will provide definitive evidence of whether BFR can protect astronaut health on long-duration spaceflights."

choices.text: Focus entirely on making the ISS study a success
Use the ISS approval to build a broader international consortium for future missions
Ensure the parallel impact streams are maintained and documented

bfr_enterprise_partnership.title: University Enterprise
bfr_enterprise_partnership.narrative:
You hand the commercialisation strand to Northumbria's enterprise team. They handle the market analysis, licensing negotiations, and business development, freeing you to focus on research and impact.

A commercial BFR training programme for physiotherapists is developed as a continuing professional development offering through the university. NHS rehabilitation departments begin adopting standardised BFR protocols based on your research.

Meanwhile, the space work continues to progress.

choices.text: Focus on the space application. The clinical adoption is self-sustaining
Document the clinical adoption as a parallel impact stream for REF
Track NHS adoption as it accelerates nationally

bfr_commercial_product.title: The Product Path
bfr_commercial_product.narrative:
You develop a commercial BFR product aimed at clinical rehabilitation and sports performance. Working with the device manufacturer, you create a consumer version of the personalised tourniquet system. Simpler than the space-qualified device but based on the same technology.

The product launches and is adopted by private physiotherapy clinics and sports performance centres. Revenue feeds back into the research programme.

The commercial success does demonstrate economic impact, but at what cost to the headline space narrative?

choices.text: Refocus on the space application before the window closes
Balance both. The multi-sector impact story is stronger for including commercial outcomes

bfr_sport_deep.title: Deep in Sport Science
bfr_sport_deep.narrative:
You fully develop the sport impact pathway. Your BFR rehabilitation protocols are adopted by twelve Premier League clubs, three international football federations, and two Olympic training centres.

You publish a landmark systematic review in the British Journal of Sports Medicine. FIFA's medical committee formally incorporates BFR as a recommended rehabilitation modality for anterior cruciate ligament injuries.

But the space opportunity still beckons, and the sport evidence makes your case to UKSA even stronger.

choices.text: Pivot to the space application, using sport evidence as the foundation
Document the sport impact as the primary REF case study

bfr_parallel_impact.title: Weaving the Threads
bfr_parallel_impact.narrative:
You commit to maintaining all impact pathways simultaneously. It requires careful delegation and coordination, but the result is a comprehensive impact narrative:

* Clinical: NHS rehabilitation departments using BFR protocols, with measured patient outcomes
* Sport: Premier League clubs, international federations, elite athlete recovery data
* Military: MOD adoption for injury recovery in operational environments
* Space: UKSA funding, device development, flight testing

The Impact Officer calls it "the most comprehensive multi-sector impact story I've seen at Northumbria."

choices.text: Push for a flight mission to complete the space strand
Document everything for REF. The multi-sector narrative is the case study

bfr_consortium.title: A Global Alliance
bfr_consortium.narrative:
You build an international consortium: Northumbria University, the European Space Agency, NASA, the Canadian Space Agency, Western Clinical Engineering Group, and Delfi Medical Innovations.

The consortium secures major funding to develop next-generation BFR hardware with integrated biofeedback technology, a system that can automatically adjust pressure based on physiological response during exercise in any gravity environment: micro-gravity, lunar, Martian, or Earth.

Back on Earth, the clinical and sport applications continue to grow organically, sustained by the team you've built.

choices.text: Focus the consortium on Mars mission readiness. That's the ultimate goal
Ensure the Earth-based impact streams are documented for REF alongside the space work

bfr_next_gen.title: Iterating After Flight
bfr_next_gen.narrative:
Following the successful commercial spaceflight, your research project receives £1.2 million of further funding from UKSA. The funding is part of a batch of 23 projects aimed at strengthening international space partnerships and developing national capabilities.

The project, working with Western Clinical Engineering Group, Delfi Medical Innovations, the Canadian Space Agency, ESA, and NASA, will resolve technological uncertainties related to future space applications.

"The UK is at the forefront of space innovation," UKSA's Chief Executive says, citing your project as an example of combining home-grown talent with global expertise.

choices.text: Build the full international consortium for deep-space missions
Document the full journey from clinic to cosmos for REF

bfr_ending_multisector.title: Impact Case Study: From Bedside to Orbit
bfr_ending_multisector.narrative:
You've built one of the most comprehensive multi-sector impact stories in the REF. Your blood flow restriction exercise research has transformed practice across four domains:

In clinical rehabilitation, NHS and private physiotherapy services across the UK have adopted your BFR protocols. Patients recovering from surgery and injury are regaining strength faster with less pain.

In elite sport, Premier League clubs, international football federations, and Olympic training centres use your techniques.

Congratulations! From a rehabilitation clinic in Newcastle to orbit around the Earth, your research has changed how humans maintain physical capability in the most demanding environments on (and off) the planet. This is what multi-sector research impact looks like.

bfr_ending_iss.title: Impact Case Study: The ISS Study
bfr_ending_iss.narrative:
Your dedicated ISS study produces definitive results. Over a six-month mission, astronauts using BFR exercise alongside standard protocols show significantly less muscle atrophy and bone density loss than historical controls using standard exercise alone.

The findings are published in Nature Medicine. NASA and ESA formally add BFR to their recommended countermeasure portfolio for long-duration spaceflight.

Congratulations! You've achieved the ultimate validation, your technique works in space. The ISS study represents a landmark in exercise physiology research, and its ripple effects across clinical practice, sport, and military medicine will be felt for decades.

bfr_ending_consortium.title: Impact Case Study: Beyond Low Earth Orbit
bfr_ending_consortium.narrative:
The international consortium you've built is now at the centre of human spaceflight health planning. Northumbria University, ESA, NASA, the Canadian Space Agency, UKSA, and your industry partners are developing the exercise countermeasure systems that will protect astronaut health on missions to the Moon under the Artemis programme, and eventually to Mars.

Your BFR device, which started as a clinical rehabilitation tool, has been adapted into a multi-gravity exercise system.

Congratulations! You've built a research programme that is literally changing how humanity prepares for life beyond Earth. From Newcastle to the cosmos, that's a journey worth mapping for REF.

bfr_ending_sport.title: Impact Case Study: Changing the Game
bfr_ending_sport.narrative:
Your BFR research has transformed sports rehabilitation worldwide. The evidence is comprehensive: twelve Premier League clubs, three international football federations, two Olympic training centres, and FIFA's medical committee have adopted your protocols.

Players recovering from ACL injuries return to competition significantly faster with lower re-injury rates. Post-match recovery protocols using BFR reduce markers of muscle damage.

Congratulations! You've demonstrated that a single exercise physiology innovation can transform rehabilitation practice from elite sport to everyday healthcare. The evidence base you've built is unassailable, and the impact is measured in faster recovery times for thousands of athletes and patients.

bfr_bed_rest_study.title: The Bed Rest Study
bfr_bed_rest_study.narrative:
You secure access to a dedicated bed rest facility through a European research partner. Bed rest studies are the gold standard for simulating spaceflight deconditioning on Earth, participants spend weeks lying in a head-down tilt position, which causes muscle wasting and bone loss similar to microgravity.

Your study design is elegant: twenty healthy participants, ten using BFR exercise during six weeks of bed rest, ten following standard protocols.

A visiting ESA physician reviews your data and says: "This is exactly what we need to see. Can you do this with your space-qualified hardware?"

choices.text: Repeat the study using the PTSS device to validate the space hardware
Publish the results immediately and approach UKSA for flight-readiness funding
Present the data at the Spaceflight Human Optimisation Summit in Texas

bfr_conference_circuit.title: The Conference Circuit
bfr_conference_circuit.narrative:
You present your BFR spaceflight countermeasure research at the Spaceflight Human Optimisation and Performance Summit in Texas. The audience includes NASA flight surgeons, ESA medical officers, commercial spaceflight companies, and aerospace medicine researchers from around the world.

Your presentation covers the full journey: from clinical rehabilitation evidence, through sport performance validation, to the bed rest analogue study results.

You also meet researchers from the Canadian Space Agency who are working on complementary countermeasures. A collaboration could strengthen both programmes.

choices.text: Pursue the NASA collaboration. They have the most ISS time and resources
Engage Axiom Space. Commercial missions are launching sooner
Build a multi-agency consortium including NASA, CSA, and ESA

bfr_nasa_collab.title: The NASA Connection
bfr_nasa_collab.narrative:
You formalise a research collaboration with NASA's Human Research Program at Johnson Space Center. The collaboration gives you access to NASA's extensive spaceflight physiological data, their bed rest facility, and their flight experiment infrastructure.

NASA's exercise countermeasure team has been exploring BFR independently, but your clinical and operational evidence base is far ahead.

NASA's endorsement carries enormous weight. When the world's leading space agency validates your research, every other door opens wider.

choices.text: Push for a joint ISS study through the NASA-ESA collaboration framework
Use the NASA partnership to attract UKSA co-investment
Build the broader consortium including CSA and commercial partners

bfr_nhs_adoption.title: Clinical Adoption at Scale
bfr_nhs_adoption.narrative:
While the space work progresses, clinical adoption of BFR accelerates. Your published protocols and the training programme developed through the university enterprise team reach NHS rehabilitation departments across the North East, then nationally.

A major NHS trust conducts an internal audit: patients using BFR rehabilitation protocols show a 25% reduction in time to discharge after knee replacement surgery, and patient-reported outcome measures are significantly better at six months.

But NICE processes take time, and you need to respond to their evidence requests alongside everything else.

choices.text: Prioritise the NICE engagement. National clinical guidelines would be transformative impact
Delegate the NICE work to a clinical colleague and stay focused on the space strand
Use the NHS evidence to strengthen the multi-sector impact narrative

bfr_nice_engagement.title: Into the Guidelines
bfr_nice_engagement.narrative:
You submit evidence to NICE's guideline review on post-surgical rehabilitation. The submission includes your systematic reviews, randomised controlled trials, the NHS trust audit data, and your sport performance evidence.

NICE's evidence review panel is rigorous. They scrutinise methodology, effect sizes, and applicability to the NHS population. Your evidence stands up well.

This is significant clinical impact: your research is now shaping the standard of care for millions of potential patients.

choices.text: Document this alongside the space impact for a comprehensive REF case study
Use the NICE recommendation to drive international clinical adoption

bfr_international_clinical.title: Global Clinical Impact
bfr_international_clinical.narrative:
The NICE guideline recommendation triggers international interest. Clinical rehabilitation bodies in Australia, Canada, and Scandinavia review your evidence and begin developing their own BFR guidelines.

You're invited to contribute to a World Health Organization technical consultation on post-surgical rehabilitation. Your BFR evidence is included in the background documentation.

Meanwhile, the space programme continues. The two impact streams, clinical rehabilitation and spaceflight countermeasure, reinforce each other perfectly.

choices.text: Bring both impact streams together for the definitive REF case study
Push for the space mission. Clinical impact is secure, now add the headline

bfr_mod_deep.title: Military Integration
bfr_mod_deep.narrative:
The MOD expands the BFR programme beyond the initial feasibility study. Your protocols are integrated into the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre at Stanford Hall, the UK's primary facility for military rehabilitation.

Serving personnel recovering from operational injuries use BFR as part of their structured rehabilitation pathway.

A senior military medical officer says: "This fills a gap we've had for twenty years, effective rehabilitation when you can't fly someone home to a fully equipped gym."

choices.text: Use the military evidence to strengthen the space proposal. Both involve constrained environments
Document the military adoption as a parallel impact stream
Explore collaboration between military and space BFR programmes

bfr_phd_programme.title: Building the Next Generation
bfr_phd_programme.narrative:
UKSA funds a fully-funded PhD studentship to develop BFR exercise as a spaceflight countermeasure, investigating the physiology, biomechanics, and feasibility in simulated micro-gravity, lunar, and Martian gravity. Your PhD student begins building the evidence base for missions beyond the ISS.

The studentship signals something important: the space agencies see this as a sustained research programme, not a one-off study.

The research group is growing. What started as your personal research interest is becoming an established field.

choices.text: Use the PhD data to support the flight hardware proposal
Build the team further. Recruit a postdoc to bridge clinical and space research

bfr_humans_in_space.title: The Humans in Space Challenge
bfr_humans_in_space.narrative:
You and your colleague from the Aerospace Medicine and Rehabilitation Laboratory enter the Humans in Space Challenge, a global competition run by South Korean health technology company Boryung in partnership with Axiom Space and the Aurelia Institute.

The media coverage is significant: "Northumbria University scientists win global space health challenge." 

Your university's communications team is delighted. The Vice-Chancellor mentions your work in a speech about institutional research excellence.

choices.text: Use the funding and connections to develop the space-ready device
Leverage the visibility to attract additional UKSA investment
Build relationships with the competition partners for long-term collaboration

sbl_start.title: The Retention Crisis
sbl_start.narrative:
You're a teacher educator at Northumbria University. Before joining academia, you spent over thirteen years as a classroom teacher and senior leader in primary schools in the North East. You know the reality of the job  -  not from textbooks, but from staffrooms, parents' evenings, and Ofsted inspections.

And the reality is this: one-third of teachers in England leave the profession within five years of qualifying. International data shows similar attrition rates across Europe  -  some sources suggest 28%. The reasons are well-documented: workload, behaviour management challenges, and a persistent feeling of being unprepared for what practitioners call "the bits of the job beyond teaching."

The teaching profession is in crisis. Your research could help. But where do you begin?

choices.text: Start small  -  design a pilot simulation and test it with your own students
Research what other professions do first  -  learn from medical simulation
Go big  -  write a funding bid for a national simulation programme

sbl_pilot.title: The First Simulation
sbl_pilot.narrative:
You design your first simulation scenario. The situation: a parent comes into school upset because their child has been excluded from a class trip due to unpaid contributions. The parent is angry, embarrassed, and feels their child is being punished for the family's financial situation. The student teacher must navigate the conversation  -  balancing empathy with school policy, de-escalating emotion, and finding a resolution.

But it's one scenario with one cohort. You need to scale this  -  and evidence it properly.

choices.text: Develop a full suite of simulation scenarios covering different challenge areas
Publish your pilot findings to establish an evidence base
Share the approach with departmental colleagues to get buy-in for embedding it

sbl_cross_sector.title: Learning from Medicine
sbl_cross_sector.narrative:
You visit simulation centres used in medical and nursing education at Northumbria and beyond. The sophistication is striking: high-fidelity mannequins that breathe and bleed, standardised patients (actors trained to present specific symptoms and emotional states), structured debriefing protocols developed over decades, and a robust evidence base for effectiveness.

You meet colleagues in Health and Life Sciences who use simulation extensively.

You can't just adopt medical simulation. You need to adapt it.

choices.text: Design an education-specific simulation framework drawing on medical best practice
Propose a cross-faculty collaboration between Education and Health simulation experts
Go straight to piloting  -  you've learned enough to start

sbl_big_bid.title: Running Before Walking
sbl_big_bid.narrative:
You write an ambitious funding bid to the Education Endowment Foundation for a ÃÂÃÂ£500,000 national programme of simulation-based learning for Initial Teacher Education. The proposal is well-argued and the need is clear.

The reviewers are interested but unconvinced. Their feedback is constructive but firm: "The rationale is compelling and the approach is innovative.

One positive note: the reviewers explicitly mention that the idea fills a genuine gap and encourage you to resubmit with pilot evidence. They want this to work  -  they just need you to prove it first.

choices.text: Run a rigorous pilot study to generate the evidence the funders need
Start smaller  -  seek departmental support and internal funding to build incrementally
Approach the EEF through your existing Senior Associate role for advice on what they'd fund

sbl_design_framework.title: Adapting the Model
sbl_design_framework.narrative:
Drawing on your cross-sector research, you develop a simulation framework specifically designed for teacher education. It borrows the structure of healthcare simulation but adapts the content:

* Pre-briefing: context-setting and ground rules (borrowed from medical simulation)
* Scenario: the simulated encounter, using trained actors rather than mannequins (adapted for relational complexity)
* Debrief: structured reflection using the Gibbs Reflective Cycle (adapted from clinical debriefing models)
* Transfer: explicit linking to classroom practice and professional standards (unique to education)

You have a framework. Now you need to test it properly.

choices.text: Run a formal pilot study using the framework
Share the framework with colleagues and get departmental buy-in first
Pilot it across multiple scenario types to test versatility

sbl_scenario_suite.title: The Scenario Library
sbl_scenario_suite.narrative:
Working with your team  -  a group of experienced teacher educators who between them have decades of classroom experience  -  you develop a suite of simulation scenarios targeting the most challenging aspects of early career teaching:

* A safeguarding disclosure: a child tells you something concerning during a quiet moment
* Behaviour management: managing disruptive behaviour during a lesson observation by your mentor
* A difficult parent: a parent is upset about their child's progress report and questions your competence
* EAL support: welcoming a newly arrived child with no English, communicating with their non-English-speaking parent
* Staffroom dynamics: a colleague makes an inappropriate comment about a child  -  what do you do?

How do you expand the impact beyond your own programme?

choices.text: Publish the evidence and share the framework with the national teacher education community
Explore using immersive virtual reality to make simulations more scalable
Develop a downloadable toolkit that other universities can adopt
Embed it formally in Northumbria's ITE programme and gather longitudinal data

sbl_publish_pilot.title: Building the Evidence Base
sbl_publish_pilot.narrative:
You write up your pilot findings rigorously. The paper  -  "Can simulation-based learning in Initial Teacher Education better prepare students for real-life as a teacher?"  -  reports on student confidence, self-efficacy measures, and qualitative reflections.

The findings show statistically significant improvements in students' confidence in handling challenging professional situations, and the qualitative data reveals deep reflective learning that traditional lecture-based preparation doesn't achieve.

But academic impact isn't enough for REF. You need to show that your research is changing practice beyond Northumbria.

choices.text: Build a national network of universities interested in simulation approaches
Develop more scenarios and gather stronger evidence before scaling
Approach the Education Endowment Foundation about a funded evaluation

sbl_departmental.title: Getting the Team On Board
sbl_departmental.narrative:
You present the simulation approach to your Education department colleagues at a teaching and learning away day. The reception is mixed.

The enthusiasts  -  mostly those with recent classroom experience  -  are immediately on board. They've seen students struggle with exactly the scenarios you're simulating.

But the enthusiasts become collaborators. Three colleagues volunteer to develop and deliver simulations in their own modules. You now have a small but committed simulation development team within the department.

choices.text: Embed simulation formally into the BA Primary Education programme with your team
Run a comparative study  -  simulation group vs traditional preparation  -  to convince the sceptics
Start with the willing colleagues and let the results speak for themselves

sbl_cross_faculty.title: Breaking Down Silos
sbl_cross_faculty.narrative:
You establish a cross-faculty simulation collaboration between Education, Nursing, Midwifery, and Social Work. Each discipline uses simulation differently, but the core principles are shared: safe practice space, experiential learning, structured debriefing, and building professional confidence before encountering real-world stakes.

This is both an opportunity and a risk. A university-wide strategy could amplify your impact, but it could also dilute your focus on the teacher education gap that's your core research question.

choices.text: Develop a university-wide simulation strategy  -  the institutional backing is valuable
Stay focused on teacher education  -  that's where the gap is most acute and your evidence is strongest
Do both  -  university strategy for institutional support, teacher education for research impact

sbl_eef_connection.title: The EEF Connection
sbl_eef_connection.narrative:
As a Senior Associate for the Education Endowment Foundation  -  co-leading a national project on school engagement and evidence use  -  you have an existing relationship with the organisation. You use this to have an informal conversation with the EEF's research team about simulation-based learning.

An EEF-commissioned evaluation would be transformative. It would put your approach through rigorous independent scrutiny and, if the results hold, give it a credibility stamp that the entire education sector trusts.

choices.text: Run the pilot study quickly so you can submit to the EEF evaluation pipeline
Build a stronger evidence base first  -  the EEF evaluation needs to succeed
Propose a small-scale EEF feasibility study as an intermediate step

sbl_embed.title: Embedding in the Programme
sbl_embed.narrative:
Working with your departmental allies, you formally embed simulation-based learning into the BA Primary Education programme at Northumbria. Simulation sessions are integrated at three points in the degree:

Year 1: An introductory simulation focused on basic classroom communication
Year 2: Behaviour management and parent conversation scenarios, before the main teaching placement
Year 3: Complex scenarios  -  safeguarding, SEND conversations, EAL support  -  preparing students for their final placement and the ECT year

You now have a programme-level intervention with emerging evidence. The question is how to scale beyond Northumbria.

choices.text: Publish the programme-level data and build a national network
Gather longitudinal data  -  track students into their first teaching posts
Develop a toolkit so other universities can replicate the programme structure

sbl_comparative_study.title: The Evidence Experiment
sbl_comparative_study.narrative:
You design a comparative study within your own programme. Two parallel cohorts of student teachers: one receives the simulation-based preparation; the other follows the traditional preparation pathway. Both groups complete the same placement.

The outcome measures include self-efficacy questionnaires, mentor assessments of professional competence, critical incident analyses, and six-month follow-up surveys after qualification.

You now have robust comparative evidence. This is the kind of data that funders and policymakers need.

choices.text: Publish the comparative study and approach the EEF for a national evaluation
Use the evidence to embed simulation across the full ITE programme
Share the findings nationally to build momentum

sbl_uni_strategy.title: The University Simulation Strategy
sbl_uni_strategy.narrative:
You draft a university-wide simulation strategy for Northumbria. It proposes simulation as a common pedagogical approach across all professional programmes  -  Education, Nursing, Social Work, Policing, Law.

The university's Learning and Teaching Committee adopts it. A small budget is allocated for a shared simulation suite.

But there's a tension: the university strategy is about institutional practice, while your REF impact case study needs to show external impact beyond Northumbria. You need to use the institutional platform to launch outward.

choices.text: Use the institutional platform to host a national simulation conference
Develop externally-facing resources  -  a toolkit other universities can use
Focus on gathering strong evidence from the embedded programme for external publication

sbl_vr_explore.title: Into Virtual Reality
sbl_vr_explore.narrative:
You collaborate with Northumbria's Computer Science department to explore immersive virtual reality (IVR) for teacher simulation. The potential is compelling: VR headsets could allow any student teacher, anywhere, to step into a simulated classroom and practice managing behaviour, communicating with parents, or handling safeguarding situations.

The VR work generates significant media interest and positions Northumbria as an innovator. But you need to be evidence-based about where VR adds value and where live simulation is still better.

choices.text: Develop VR for behaviour management and keep live actors for relational scenarios
Publish a realist evaluation comparing VR and live simulation
Focus on the VR approach  -  it's more scalable and generates more interest

sbl_national_share.title: Sharing the Work
sbl_national_share.narrative:
You present your work at national teacher education conferences and write accessible practice articles for the Chartered College of Teaching's Impact journal. The response from teacher educators across the UK is enthusiastic.

"We've been thinking about this too" is a common refrain. Several universities are doing informal simulation activities but none have a systematic framework, evidence base, or published approach.

There's an opportunity here to build something bigger than a single university project.

choices.text: Propose a formal National Simulation Network
Develop a toolkit that lowers the barrier to entry for other universities
Organise a national conference to bring everyone together

sbl_network_build.title: Finding Your People
sbl_network_build.narrative:
You reach out systematically to teacher educators across the UK. Through conference presentations, direct emails, and word of mouth, you identify a dozen academics who are either already experimenting with simulation or keen to start.

The interest is genuine but so are the barriers. Most universities have no dedicated simulation space for education.

These are the problems you need to solve to achieve national impact. But solving them requires collective action  -  no single university can build the infrastructure alone.

choices.text: Create a formal national network with shared governance and purpose
Develop a practical toolkit that helps others start without needing infrastructure
Seek funding for a collaborative multi-site research project

sbl_toolkit_dev.title: The Open Toolkit
sbl_toolkit_dev.narrative:
You develop a comprehensive Simulation-Based Learning Toolkit for Teacher Education. It's designed to be practical, accessible, and usable by any ITE provider regardless of their resources:

* Scenario templates for six core professional challenges
* Actor/role player briefing cards with responsive improvisation guidance
* Facilitation guides with step-by-step session plans
* Debrief protocols aligned to reflective practice frameworks
* Assessment rubrics linked to the Teachers' Standards
* A quick-start guide for departments with no prior simulation experience
* Video exemplars showing how to run each type of session

One programme director writes: "Your toolkit gave us permission to try something we'd been talking about for years. It lowered the barrier enough that even our sceptics agreed to pilot one session."

choices.text: Track adoption data and gather feedback for a formal impact evaluation
Use the adoption to launch a formal national network
Iterate the toolkit based on user feedback and develop version 2.0

sbl_network_launch.title: The National Simulation Network
sbl_network_launch.narrative:
You formally launch the National Simulation Network  -  a collaborative group of academics from universities across the UK dedicated to promoting simulation-based approaches for Initial Teacher Education and teacher professional learning.

The network launches with twelve member institutions. You're elected as Chair. The founding meeting establishes three working groups:

1. Research: developing a shared evidence framework and collaborative research agenda

This is where individual research becomes systemic change. What do you prioritise through the network?

choices.text: Develop national standards for simulation in teacher education
Use the network to engage DfE about including simulation in ITT guidance
Commission a multi-site research study through the network
Develop a VR platform accessible to all network members

sbl_eef_feasibility.title: The EEF Study
sbl_eef_feasibility.narrative:
The Education Endowment Foundation commissions a feasibility study of your simulation-based learning approach. This is significant  -  an EEF evaluation is the gold standard in UK education evidence.

The study design involves six universities: three using your simulation framework, three acting as comparison sites using their existing preparation approaches.

The EEF report is read by every ITE provider in the country. Your approach now has independent, credible validation.

choices.text: Push for a full-scale randomised controlled trial through the EEF
Use the EEF report to engage DfE about recognition in ITT frameworks
Scale adoption through the National Simulation Network using the EEF evidence

sbl_longitudinal.title: Tracking Into Teaching
sbl_longitudinal.narrative:
You design a longitudinal study tracking students from their simulation experiences at Northumbria through their first three years of teaching. The study measures professional confidence, self-efficacy, critical incident management, and  -  crucially  -  retention in the profession.

The retention data is the headline. If simulation-based learning can demonstrably reduce early career attrition, the economic case alone is compelling  -  it costs approximately ÃÂÃÂ£30,000 to recruit and train a new teacher.

choices.text: Publish the retention data and take it to the DfE
Use the data to secure EEF funding for a national evaluation
Share the findings with the National Simulation Network to drive adoption

sbl_hybrid_approach.title: Best of Both Worlds
sbl_hybrid_approach.narrative:
You develop a hybrid simulation model: VR for behaviour management and classroom environment scenarios (where the technology excels at creating immersive, repeatable experiences), and live actors for relational scenarios (parent conversations, safeguarding disclosures, colleague interactions) where emotional authenticity is essential.

The hybrid approach is more versatile than either method alone.

You publish the hybrid model in the Journal of Applied Learning and Teaching, including a realist evaluation protocol for further testing.

choices.text: Share the VR component through the National Simulation Network
Develop the VR platform into a product that any university can license
Focus on the evidence  -  run a formal evaluation of VR vs live vs hybrid

sbl_vr_evaluation.title: The Evidence Comparison
sbl_vr_evaluation.narrative:
You publish a realist evaluation comparing three simulation modalities: immersive VR, live actor simulation, and the hybrid approach. The study examines not just effectiveness but the mechanisms  -  what works, for whom, in what circumstances.

The findings are nuanced. VR is most effective for practising procedural responses (behaviour management steps, safeguarding protocols).

The paper is published in the Journal of Applied Learning and Teaching and becomes a reference point for the emerging field of simulation in teacher education.

choices.text: Use the evidence to develop national standards for simulation quality
Focus on training facilitators  -  the debrief finding suggests that's where the real skill lies
Share the comparative evidence to help network members choose the right approach

sbl_vr_full.title: The VR Classroom
sbl_vr_full.narrative:
You commit fully to the VR approach. Working with Computer Science colleagues and a small EdTech company, you develop a suite of VR classroom simulations. The virtual environment is detailed: a primary classroom with twenty pupil avatars, each with distinct behavioural profiles.

Student teachers can practice in the virtual classroom repeatedly, experimenting with different strategies.

But the evidence needs to keep pace with the excitement. Does the VR experience actually translate to improved real-world classroom performance? Initial data is promising but you need more.

choices.text: Run a rigorous evaluation before scaling further
Scale through the network while gathering evidence in parallel
Present at DfE to show innovative approaches to teacher preparation

sbl_national_conference.title: Bringing the Community Together
sbl_national_conference.narrative:
You organise a national conference at Northumbria: "Simulation for Teacher Education: Evidence, Practice, and Policy." It brings together teacher educators, simulation specialists from healthcare, Ofsted inspectors, DfE representatives, and EdTech developers.

The conference is a success. Over 120 delegates attend. Panel discussions reveal a strong consensus: teacher education needs to innovate, and simulation offers a credible, evidence-based approach.

The conference generates momentum and connections. It's a catalyst for formalising the national network.

choices.text: Use the conference momentum to formally launch the National Simulation Network
Follow up with the DfE official to explore policy recognition
Develop a post-conference collaborative research bid with interested universities

sbl_multisite_study.title: Collaborative Evidence
sbl_multisite_study.narrative:
Through the network, you design a multi-site research study. Eight universities implement simulation-based learning using your framework, with a shared research protocol and common outcome measures.

The scale gives you statistical power that a single-site study can't match.

The collaborative paper, with authors from eight institutions, is submitted to a top education journal. It's the most comprehensive evidence base for simulation in teacher education that exists anywhere in the world.

choices.text: Take the evidence to the DfE for policy recognition
Use it to develop national quality standards
Submit the evidence base to the EEF for a full-scale evaluation

sbl_toolkit_impact.title: Measuring Toolkit Adoption
sbl_toolkit_impact.narrative:
You systematically track adoption of your open-access toolkit. After twelve months, the data tells a compelling story:

* 23 universities have downloaded the toolkit
* 14 are actively using at least one scenario
* 8 have embedded simulation into their programmes
* 3 have adapted and expanded the scenarios for their local context
* Over 400 student teachers have experienced simulation-based preparation

The toolkit has created practice change at scale. For REF, this is powerful impact evidence  -  your research is directly shaping teacher preparation across the UK.

choices.text: Document this as the primary REF impact evidence
Address the barriers  -  develop facilitator training to support further adoption
Use the adoption data to make the case to DfE for formal recognition

sbl_toolkit_v2.title: Learning from Users
sbl_toolkit_v2.narrative:
You gather feedback from toolkit users and develop version 2.0. The improvements are driven by real-world use:

* Simplified scenario cards that work without trained actors (peers can play the roles)
* A video demonstration library showing facilitation in practice
* Additional scenarios developed by network members, quality-assured against your framework
* Assessment rubrics explicitly mapped to the new Teachers' Standards
* A facilitator self-study guide for educators with no simulation experience

Adoption accelerates. Twenty-seven universities are now using some element of the toolkit.

choices.text: Launch the facilitator training as a formal CPD programme
Document the national adoption for REF
Use the momentum to push for DfE recognition

sbl_rct.title: The Gold Standard Trial
sbl_rct.narrative:
The EEF commissions a full-scale randomised controlled trial of your simulation-based learning approach. It's the largest study of simulation in teacher education ever conducted in the UK: thirty ITE providers, fifteen using simulation, fifteen as comparison.

The trial runs over three years, tracking student teachers from training through their first years of teaching.

The EEF publishes the trial as evidence of "moderate to strong" impact. The report is downloaded by every ITE provider in England.

choices.text: Take the RCT evidence to DfE as the definitive case for policy change
Use the evidence to drive universal adoption through the network

sbl_facilitator_training.title: Training the Trainers
sbl_facilitator_training.narrative:
You develop a certified Simulation Facilitation Training programme for teacher educators, accredited through Northumbria University's CPD framework. The two-day intensive course covers scenario design, role player management, facilitation skills, and  -  drawing on your research finding that debriefing is the key mechanism  -  advanced debriefing techniques.

The first three cohorts train 45 teacher educators from across the UK.

Several universities now include simulation facilitation in their staff development requirements for ITE tutors.

choices.text: Scale the training nationally through the network
Use the trained facilitator network to push for formal recognition

sbl_vr_platform.title: Scaling Through Technology
sbl_vr_platform.narrative:
Working with your EdTech partner, you develop a VR simulation platform that any university can access through a licensing agreement. The platform includes the classroom behaviour management simulations your team developed, with new scenarios being added based on network feedback.

The technology removes several adoption barriers: universities don't need simulation space, trained actors, or experienced facilitators for the VR component.

The platform generates modest revenue that feeds back into your research programme. But more importantly, it provides scalable access to simulation for student teachers across the country.

choices.text: Document the platform adoption as technology transfer impact
Combine VR data with live simulation evidence for a comprehensive policy case

sbl_standards.title: Setting the Standard
sbl_standards.narrative:
Through the National Simulation Network, you co-develop national quality standards for simulation-based learning in teacher education. The standards draw on your research evidence, cross-sector learning from healthcare simulation, and the collective practice wisdom of network members.

For the first time, there's a shared language and quality framework for simulation in teacher education. Universities can design, deliver, and evaluate simulation with confidence that they're meeting nationally recognised standards.

choices.text: Push for DfE to include simulation in their ITT curriculum framework
Document the standards adoption as the core REF impact narrative

sbl_dfe_engage.title: Into the Policy Arena
sbl_dfe_engage.narrative:
You engage with the Department for Education through multiple channels: the National Simulation Network submits a formal response to the ITT Market Review; you present at a DfE-hosted innovation showcase; and your EEF evidence is cited in policy briefings.

The DfE's response is cautiously encouraging.

It's not a mandate, but it's recognition. Providers can now cite DfE guidance when justifying simulation in their programmes. For institutions where senior leadership has been reluctant, this removes a significant barrier.

choices.text: Use the DfE recognition to accelerate network adoption
Push further  -  aim for simulation to be a required element in ITT
Focus on documenting the full impact journey for REF

sbl_ending_toolkit.title: Impact Case Study: Open Source Impact
sbl_ending_toolkit.narrative:
Your freely available Simulation-Based Learning Toolkit has been adopted by teacher education programmes across the UK and internationally. Twenty-seven universities use your scenarios and framework. Over 1,200 student teachers have experienced simulation-based preparation using your materials.

The toolkit's open-access model has demonstrated something important: impact doesn't require commercialisation.

Congratulations! You've achieved practice-based impact at national scale. From a single pilot simulation with drama students playing upset parents, you've built a replicable, evidence-based approach to teacher preparation that's being adopted across the country  -  addressing the preparation gap that contributes to the teaching profession's retention crisis.

sbl_ending_standards.title: Impact Case Study: Setting the Standard
sbl_ending_standards.narrative:
From a single pilot simulation in a repurposed seminar room, you've built a national framework that's reshaping how the UK prepares its teachers.

The National Simulation Network, which you chair, now includes twenty-five universities. The national quality standards you co-developed are referenced by Ofsted in their ITT inspection framework and endorsed by the Chartered College of Teaching and UCET.

Congratulations! You've achieved systemic impact. The teacher retention crisis won't be solved by one intervention alone  -  but giving new teachers safe, supported space to practise the hardest parts of the job before they encounter them for real is a powerful, evidence-based contribution. And you've built the infrastructure to sustain it.

sbl_ending_policy.title: Impact Case Study: Into the Framework
sbl_ending_policy.narrative:
Your sustained engagement with evidence, practice, and policy has achieved something rare: a new pedagogical approach has been recognised in national education policy within a single REF cycle.

The Department for Education's updated ITT guidance explicitly references simulation-based learning.

Congratulations! You've achieved policy-level impact in education. From an idea borrowed from medical simulation and adapted through rigorous, practice-informed research, you've helped create a nationally recognised approach to teacher preparation that addresses one of education's most pressing challenges. Student teachers across the country are entering the profession better prepared, more confident, and more likely to stay.

greetings.early: You're just getting started and that's a great time to check in. The decisions you make early on shape everything that follows.
greetings.mid: You're building momentum. Let's make sure you're heading in the right direction and not missing any opportunities.
greetings.late: You've made quite a few decisions now. Let's take stock of where you are and what the strongest next move might be.

phaseAdvice.planning: You're still in the planning phase. That's fine, rushing into engagement without a strategy is one of the most common mistakes researchers make. Take your time mapping stakeholders and pathways. A good Theory of Change now saves months of wasted effort later.
phaseAdvice.evidence: You're focused on building evidence. Strong evidence is the foundation of everything, but don't forget that the best evidence in the world doesn't create impact on its own. You need people who'll champion it, use it, and act on it. Think about who those people are while you're building the case.
phaseAdvice.engagement: You're in active engagement with stakeholders. This is where relationships are built. Remember: listen at least as much as you present. Understanding their priorities is as important as sharing your findings. The best impact stories come from genuine two-way relationships, not one-way presentations.
phaseAdvice.translation: You're translating research into practical outputs, frameworks, toolkits, guidelines. These are what practitioners actually use day-to-day. Make sure they're co-designed with the people who'll use them, not just handed down from the university. Co-production isn't just good practice, it's better impact.
phaseAdvice.adoption: Your work is being adopted by others. This is exciting but fragile, early adoption needs nurturing. Stay close to the people implementing your work, learn from their experience, and be ready to iterate. The first version is rarely the final one.
phaseAdvice.scaling: You're at the scaling stage, this is where individual impact becomes systemic change. Think about sustainability: what happens when you're not personally driving this? Networks, standards, and institutional embedding are what make impact last beyond a single project.

categoryTips.strategy: Think about your Theory of Change. Can you draw a clear line from your research to the change you want to see in the world? If you can't explain it in two sentences, it's not sharp enough yet. That's what we can help with.
categoryTips.stakeholders: Who are the people with the power to make change happen? Not just who's interested in your research, who can actually act on it? Policymakers, practitioners, commissioners, professional bodies. Map them, understand their priorities, and build relationships before you need them.
categoryTips.significance: For REF, significance means the degree of change your research has brought about. A small change affecting many people, or a large change affecting fewer people, are both valid, but you need to be clear which you're aiming for and have evidence to demonstrate it.
categoryTips.reach: Reach isn't just about numbers. It's about how far beyond academia your work extends. Media coverage, policy citations, practice adoption, public awareness, each extends your reach in different ways. Think about which channels matter most for your particular research.
categoryTips.evidence: Impact evidence needs to be more than 'people liked our workshop.' Think about what actually changed as a result of engaging with your research. Behaviour change, policy change, practice change, new products or services, that's what REF panels are looking for. Start collecting evidence now, not retrospectively.
